Grace always says that small steps matter more than big plans. The bird-watching spot has become an important part of daily life. Ben believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. He intends to study abroad next year.
Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. The experience taught Ben more than any book could. Best of all, a wild corner beats a mowed lawn.

There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. The flower market looked quieter than usual that evening. Ben bought a dress online because it was much cheaper. What's more, invasive species crowd out native river fish.

Ben has practiced table tennis for three years and won a prize last term. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. On Thursday evenings, Ben reviews the notes from class. Ginny painted her first watercolor of the harbor last weekend.
There are always more possibilities than we expect. Ben is saving money to buy a ticket to Xi'an. Little by little, things began to change.
